title: The Visitor of the Undercroft
premise: Ivo Zhou, a pest controller who prides themselves on never believing in anything, is called to Fenwick House to deal with 'something with fingerprints' — smudges appearing on the inside of sealed windows, on ceilings, on the skin of the sleeping. The house belongs to three estranged siblings who inherited it from a grandmother they barely knew, and beneath it lies an undercroft where, generations ago, the family silenced a wronged servant by erasing her name from every record and every memory. As the mirrors begin lagging one second behind reality, Ivo realizes the house is replaying that erasure on a loop, and the fingerprints belong to someone trying to be remembered before the house finishes forgetting her forever. To end it, Ivo — who has spent their life refusing to belong to any family — must help the siblings learn the lullaby's final verse, the one that names her, without singing along themselves; the last verse restores her name, frees the house, and leaves Ivo with an inheritance they never expected: a chosen family and a grave finally marked.
about_author: Kestrel Zhou is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade crawling through the cellars of old English houses and never once went alone again. They write horror about the debts families leave behind in walls, floorboards, and names.

chapters.title: Something With Fingerprints
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A routine call to Fenwick House: smudges on the inside of sealed windows, arranged like pressed palms. Ivo, dryly skeptical, inspects the undercroft door and finds it warm. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a lifetime of refusing to care about anyone or anything that might disappear.

chapters.title: The Three Heirs
chapters.summary: POV alternating among siblings Margot, Dev, and Cass, reunited for the funeral reading. The will grants them the house jointly — none may sell without all agreeing — and mentions a 'tenant below' whose rent was paid in song. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into unease as each admits they heard humming as children.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Overnight in the house to monitor 'activity.' At 3:07 a.m., every mirror reflects the room a full second behind — and in that second, a figure stands where no one stands. Ivo photographs it; the photos show empty rooms. Emotional beat: skepticism cracking into terror they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: POV Cass. The siblings force the undercroft door and find a bricked alcove, a child's shoe, and a wall covered in handprints — small, adult-sized, decades old. The temperature drops when spoken to rudely. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; Cass remembers being told never to sing in the house.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Paid
chapters.summary: POV Margot, digging through parish records and a locked writing desk. She uncovers the story of Edith Vane, a servant accused of theft in 1911, walled in the undercroft alive, her name struck from registers. Emotional beat: horror at inheritance — the house itself is the family's confession.

chapters.title: The Song Without Its End
chapters.summary: POV Dev. A music box recovered from the desk plays a lullaby that stops mid-phrase; whenever it does, the mirrors lag longer, and wet footprints climb one stair higher each night. Dev, a failed musician, recognizes the melody as one their mother hummed. Emotional beat: dread becoming personal — the family has been singing the erasure for generations.

chapters.title: Do Not Sing Along
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The house begins completing the verse through its inhabitants: Margot hums it asleep, Cass mouths it in mirrors. Ivo realizes the trap — the song wants voices to finish it, which would seal Edith permanently. Emotional beat: Ivo, who believes in nothing, chooses to believe in protecting these strangers.

chapters.title: The Night the Mirrors Caught Up
chapters.summary: POV rotating through all four. The lag closes to zero; the house replays 1911 around them — lantern light, masonry dust, a woman's voice asking who will say her name. Cass nearly sings the ending. Emotional beat: climax of fear; the past is no longer behind them but around them.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the undercroft, the siblings speak — not sing — Edith Vane's name into the silence while Ivo holds the line against the house pulling them toward the melody. The wall breathes out; the handprints fade; the mirrors reflect only the present. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice delivered outside any law, by witness alone.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, weeks later. The siblings sell nothing; instead they mark Edith's grave and keep the house as something shared. Ivo, invited to stay for dinner and then indefinitely, accepts for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — found family, a name restored, and a pest controller who finally believes in belonging.
